circumstances: The researcher sends the bounded methods note to a collaborator and then works on a final pre-circulation pass. Feedback arrives later in the day: the collaborator questions whether the term 'robustness' is too strong and asks for a clearer distinction between prevalence-estimation noise and actual prevalence shift. The researcher checks the cited papers and the pilot configuration, then revises terminology and adds a small clarification to the methods section. They also discover that one figure caption implies a comparison that was not actually performed and correct it. A short attempt to formulate a broader follow-up question is parked after the researcher realizes it would require new datasets and assumptions. The day ends with the revised note ready for another read-through.

activities.title: Prepare and circulate the bounded methods note

key_observations: The bounded methods note was circulated and received substantive feedback focused on terminology and scope rather than missing experiments.
The distinction between prevalence-estimation noise and prevalence shift needed to be made explicit, and the wording around 'robustness' was appropriately weakened.
A figure caption was corrected because it implied a comparison that the pilot had not actually performed.
A possible broader multi-dataset study was identified but correctly separated from the current note.
The revised note is now ready for another focused read-through rather than another round of experimental expansion.
priority_alignment: The main deliverable remained the bounded methods note.
Collaborator feedback was addressed through interpretation and documentation changes instead of automatically triggering new experiments.
Future research was kept separate from the current scope.
important_uncertainty: The current pilot still does not establish generality across datasets.
The distinction between prevalence-estimation noise and actual prevalence shift may need to remain explicit in future versions.
It is not yet clear whether the collaborator will consider the revised framing sufficient.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Do one final focused read-through of the revised note, then send the updated version back to the collaborator if no further unsupported claims remain.

primary_action.title: Close the collaborator revision loop
primary_action.reason: The requested changes are concrete and already implemented; the next useful step is a final read-through and return to the collaborator rather than reopening the study.

secondary_action.title: Keep the broader study parked
secondary_action.reason: The broader multi-dataset idea is plausible but would introduce new assumptions and scope beyond the current bounded note.

things_not_to_do: Do not add experiments just because the collaborator questioned terminology.
Do not use 'robustness' as a stronger claim than the pilot supports.
Do not conflate prevalence-estimation noise with actual prevalence shift.
Do not let the future multi-dataset study replace finishing the current note.
